epsilon),       size = 1     )   # epsilon-decreasing   } else if (i > threshold & is.na(epsilon) & !(is.na(lambda))) {     try <- sample(       c(1, 0),       prob = c(         1 / (1 + lambda * i),          lambda * i / (1 + lambda * i)       ),       size = 1     )   }   else {     try <- "ERROR"   }      return(try) } print(binaryRL::func_pi) func_gamma <- function(   # variables before decision-making   i, L_freq, R_freq, L_pick, R_pick, L_value, R_value,   # adjusting Left option value or Right option  value   LR,   # parameters   pi,    # extra variables   var1, var2,    # extra parameters   alpha, beta  ){   if (!(LR %in% c("L", "R"))) {     stop("LR = 'L' or 'R'")   } ############################# [ adjust value ] #################################   else if (LR == "L") {     bias <- pi * sqrt(log(L_pick + exp(1)) / (L_pick + 1e-10))   }   else if (LR == "R") {     bias <- pi * sqrt(log(R_pick + exp(1)) / (R_pick + 1e-10))   } ################################# [ error ] ####################################   else {     bias <- "ERROR"   }      return(bias) } print(binaryRL::func_tau) func_tau <- function (   # variables before decision-making   i, L_freq, R_freq, L_pick, R_pick, L_value, R_value,    # Exploration–Exploitation Trade-off      try,   # calculating Left option or Right option probability   LR,   # parameters   tau,    # extra variables   var1, var2,    # extra parameters   alpha, beta  ){   if (!(LR %in% c("L", "R"))) {     stop("LR = 'L' or 'R'")   }   else if (try == 0 & LR == "L") {     prob <- 1 / (1 + exp(-(L_value - R_value) * tau))   }   else if (try == 0 & LR == "R") {     prob <- 1 / (1 + exp(-(R_value - L_value) * tau))   }   else if (try == 1) {     prob <- 0.5   }    else {     prob <- "ERROR"   }    return(prob) }

title: Functions
text: \[ \textbf{Markov Decision Process (MDP)} \] \[ V_{\text{new}}(S_t) \leftarrow V_{\text{old}}(S_t) + \eta \cdot \left[ r_{t+1} + \gamma r_{t+2} + \gamma^2 r_{t+3} + \dots + \gamma^{T - t - 1} r_T - V_{\text{old}}(S_t) \right] \] \[ \Downarrow \] \[ \quad \text{(bootstrapping future rewards value estimates)} \] \[ \Downarrow \] \[ \textbf{Temporal-Difference TD(0)} \] \[ V_{\text{new}}(S_t) \leftarrow V_{\text{old}}(S_t) + \eta \cdot \left[   r_{t+1} + \gamma V_{\text{old}}(S_{t+1}) - V_{\text{old}}(S_t) \right] \] \[ \Downarrow \] \[ \quad \text{(future value estimation)} \] \[ \Downarrow \] \[ \textbf{Rescorla-Wagner Model} \] \[ V_{\text{new}}(S_t) \leftarrow V_{\text{old}}(S_t) + \eta \cdot \left[r_{t+1} - V_{\text{old}}(S_t) \right] \]

title: Functions
text: People’s subjective perception objective rewards accurate. relationship physical quantities psychological quantities necessarily always linear discount function; also another type power function relationship (Stevens’ Power Law). \[   U(r) = r^{\gamma}   \] According Kahneman’s Prospect Theory, individuals exhibit distinct utility functions gains losses. Referencing Nilsson et al. (2012), implemented model . replacing util_func specified form follows, can enable model run utility function based Kahneman’s Prospect Theory. \[ U(R) = \begin{cases}   -\beta \cdot (-R)^{\gamma_{1}}, & \text{} x \le 0   \\   R^{\gamma_{2}}, & \text{} x > 0 \end{cases} \] NOTE: Although traditional reinforcement learning model utilize symbol \(\gamma\), interpretation differs. traditional RL, \(\gamma\) serves discount rate future rewards. contrast, within package, \(\gamma\) functions parameter utility function.

title: Functions
text: parameter \(\eta\) controls quickly agent updates value estimates based new information. closer learning rate 1, aggressively value updated, giving greater credence immediate reward rather previously learned value. \[ \eta(p) = \begin{cases}   \eta, &  |\mathbf{p}| = 1 \quad \text{(TD)}   \\   \eta_{-}; \eta_{+}, &  |\mathbf{p}| = 2 \quad \text{(RDTD)} \end{cases} \] NOTE: ’s one \(\eta\) parameter, corresponds TD model. two \(\eta\) parameters, refers RSTD model.

title: Functions
text: parameter \(\epsilon\) represents probability participants engaging exploration (random choosing). addition threshold ensures participants always explore initial trials, likelihood exploration determined \(\epsilon\)..

title: Functions
text: \[ P(x) = \begin{cases}   trial \le threshold, &  x = 1 \quad \text{(random choosing)}   \\   trial > threshold, &  x = 0 \quad \text{(value-based choosing)} \end{cases} \]

title: Functions
text: \[ P(x) = \begin{cases}   \epsilon, &  x = 1 \quad \text{(random choosing)}   \\   1 - \epsilon, &  x = 0 \quad \text{(value-based choosing)} \end{cases} \]

title: Functions
text: \[ P(x) = \begin{cases}   \frac{1}{1 + \lambda }, &  x = 1 \quad \text{(random choosing)}   \\   \frac{\lambda }{1 + \lambda }, &  x = 0 \quad \text{(value-based choosing)} \end{cases} \]

title: Functions
text: Parameter used Upper-Confidence-Bound (UCB) action selection formula. controls degree exploration scaling uncertainty bonus given less-explored options. \[ A_t = \arg \max_{} \left[ V_t() + \pi \sqrt{\frac{\ln(t)}{N_t()}} \right] \]

title: Functions
text: parameter \(\tau\) represents people’s sensitivity value differences. larger \(\tau\), sensitive differences value two options. \[ P_{L} = \frac{1}{1 + e^{-(V_{L} - V_{R}) \cdot \tau}} \quad \quad P_{R} = \frac{1}{1 + e^{-(V_{R} - V_{L}) \cdot \tau}} \]
